name: Schembil
description: Schembil is a six-player partnership trick-taking game and variant of Briscola, played in Northern Africa and Southern Italy (especially Sicily). Two teams of three choose a captain (rais) who may direct partners; 36 cards (40-card pack minus twos), three cards each, replenish from stock after each trick.

Country/Region of Origin: Europe
Time Period: Early 1900s
Historical Development: The game evolved from traditional card games in the region
Cultural Significance: Popular social and family game

Minimum Players: 2
Maximum Players: 6
Optimal Players: 6
Partnerships: Yes (two teams of three)

Type: 36 cards from Italian 40-card pack (twos omitted)
Number of Decks: 1
Jokers: Not included

Italian 40-card deck (use 36 cards)
Score sheet (optional)
Table space

Cards per Player: 3 each
Dealing Pattern: Clockwise
Replenish: Each player draws one card from stock at end of each trick until stock exhausted
